artifacts.summary: Gate 8 now passes --fail-on-new and branches three ways (pass/warn_advisory/fail) on run-all.sh's own EXPECTED/NEW accounting; new fixture regression suite (22 assertions), roster-header format-stability pin, consumer re-verification, and documentation convergence all landed; redeployed and scoped-verified.

completion_data.completion_summary: Gave verify-deploy.sh's Gate 8 a three-way verdict (pass/warn_advisory/fail) driven by run-all.sh's existing --fail-on-new accounting, so an all-declared-expected failing run is non-blocking and visible rather than a bare FAIL. Added a fixture regression suite (22 assertions across 4 required shapes, consumer-level checks, and non-vacuousness probes), a roster-header format-stability pin, documentation of the new semantics and its accepted mixed-failure residual, and redeployed with a scoped post-deploy verification pass.

memory_candidates.content: When a verify-deploy.sh gate wraps a child tool that already computes an expected-vs-new (or similarly graded) classification of its own failures, give the gate a three-way verdict (pass/warn_advisory/fail) that consumes the child's existing flag/output rather than re-deriving the classification. Use warn_advisory() (not plain warn() or pass()) for the non-blocking-but-visible branch: it increments CHECKS (avoiding the zero-check-under-filter exit-2 branch under --only-gate), appends to GATE_DIRTY_LIST (preserving --skip-unchanged cache-invalidation so a warm PASS is never cached over a genuinely-failing corpus), and emits a WARN-FINDING line that deploy_findings_snapshot's strict grep '^FINDING ' filter does not match -- so the outcome never reaches a batch-blocking pre/post findings comparison. Discriminate the clean-vs-graded-failure cases by the PRESENCE of a stable marker line (never a numeric tally), choosing the degrade direction so a format change degrades to under-reporting (safe) rather than silently swallowing a real failure.

generate-context-line-counts.sh refuses to run from the agent-system source-store scripts/ directory (its own relative repo-root resolution would be bogus there) and must be invoked via the DEPLOYED copy (.claude/scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh --write) -- but it still writes the corrected line_count back into the SOURCE STORE's own index-entries.json (e.g. agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json), not a deployed-tree file. A doc edit that grows/shrinks a file under agent-system/**/context/ needs this repair before gate 3 (doc-lint)'s Rule R passes, and the repair call itself must go through the deployed path even though its effect lands in source.

When /orchestrate runs a multi-task batch, a dispatch's full, unscoped verify-deploy.sh run can surface NEW test failures in suites completely outside that dispatch's own file_scope -- confirmed via git log to belong to unrelated, already-completed tasks -- alongside several minutes of specs/.gate-lock contention from a concurrent sibling session. This is exactly the scenario a dispatch file's 'Batch Gate Deferral' directive exists to handle: close the phase against a SCOPED --only-gate/--only invocation covering only the files that phase actually touched, record that the full battery was deferred to the once-per-batch stage, and do not treat an unrelated suite's failure as this task's own defect to fix or exclude.
